# Refining Features with Claude — Research Report

## How people approach refining features with Claude

Across Anthropic's official docs, its internal-usage reports, and a wide range of practitioner write-ups, one consensus picture emerges, and it follows the talk's loop almost exactly.

The single organizing constraint is the context window: "Most best practices are based on one constraint: Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills" ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)). Almost every technique is downstream of managing that finite, high-signal budget.

From there the consensus loop is:

- **Separate research/planning from implementation.** Explore in read-only plan mode first, because "letting Claude jump straight to coding can produce code that solves the wrong problem" ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)). The canonical shape is **Explore → Plan → Code → Commit**.
- **Capture the plan or spec as a reviewable artifact** (a plan you edit with Ctrl+G, or a self-contained `SPEC.md`) and execute it in a fresh session with clean context.
- **Give Claude a check it can run** — tests, build exit code, linter, fixture diff, or a screenshot to compare. This is repeatedly called the highest-leverage practice: without it, "looks done" is the only signal and you become the verification loop ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)).
- **Treat Claude as a fast, fallible junior engineer, not a one-shot oracle.** Anthropic's RL team reports one-shot prompts work "about one-third of the time"; Sanity's staff engineer treats the first attempt as "~95% garbage" that builds context rather than delivers ([Anthropic teams](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/58284b19e702b49db9302d5b6f135ad8871e7658.pdf), [Sanity](https://www.sanity.io/blog/first-attempt-will-be-95-garbage)).
- **Verify with a fresh, independent context** — an adversarial reviewer that sees only the diff and the criteria, "so the agent doing the work isn't the one grading it" ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)).
- **Persist context that compounds** — a lean `CLAUDE.md`, plus learnings folded back in for the next cycle.

The role shift is real and measured: at Anthropic, feature-implementation work rose from 14.3% to 36.9% of Claude Code usage (Feb–Aug 2025), merged PRs per engineer per day rose 67%, and one engineer described "70%+ [shifting] to being a code reviewer/reviser rather than a net-new code writer" ([Anthropic research](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-ai-is-transforming-work-at-anthropic)). The human increasingly scopes, plans, and verifies rather than types.

## Techniques worth featuring in the talk

Grouped by the phase each fits best. Several techniques span phases; each appears once under its dominant phase with cross-phase use noted.

### Pick

**The one-sentence skip rule.**
Plan-mode ceremony is overhead, so don't always pay it: "If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan." Plan when the approach is uncertain, the change spans multiple files, or you're unfamiliar with the code. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [codewithmukesh](https://codewithmukesh.com/blog/plan-mode-claude-code/))
*When/why:* Decide before you start whether a backlog item even warrants the full loop.

**Scope to small, verifiable, low-risk slices.**
Pick work that is self-contained and objectively verifiable (build + tests). Faros deliberately chose a 200+ file tech-debt refactor because it had low business-logic risk and was build-verifiable. ([Faros](https://www.faros.ai/blog/claude-code-for-tech-debt), [Anthropic research](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-ai-is-transforming-work-at-anthropic))
*When/why:* The work you can delegate cleanly is the work that is easy to check.

**Whole-backlog audit before refining individual tickets.**
Point Claude (via the Atlassian MCP) at the backlog to surface missing descriptions, duplicates, stale items, and hidden thematic clusters before grooming any single ticket. One PO had Claude find that "90% of items were implementation-focused." ([daniel-inka](https://daniel-inka.medium.com/how-claude-ai-and-jira-mcp-helped-me-onboard-faster-as-a-new-produdct-owner-b82d13592573), [mindstudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/claude-code-jira-mcp-sprint-planning-automation))

### Research

**Explore in read-only plan mode (agentic search, not a stale index).**
Toggle plan mode (Shift+Tab or `--permission-mode plan`); Claude reads files, greps, and follows references like an engineer rather than querying a pre-built RAG/vector index — favoring freshness, precision, and privacy. Anthropic dropped its early RAG + local vector DB because "agentic search generally works better." ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [large codebases](https://claude.com/blog/how-claude-code-works-in-large-codebases-best-practices-and-where-to-start), [vadim.blog](https://vadim.blog/claude-code-no-indexing/))
*When/why:* Build a grounded mental model of the feature area before any edits. Caveat: grep misses renamed symbols and high-cardinality searches blow up context — add an LSP/code-intelligence plugin or a semantic-search MCP for conceptual queries.

**Delegate investigation to subagents that return summaries.**
A subagent explores in its own context window and returns only a distilled summary (Anthropic cites ~1,000–2,000 tokens), keeping the main conversation clean. Prompt: "Use subagents to investigate how our auth system handles token refresh and whether we have OAuth utilities to reuse." ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [effective context engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents))
*When/why:* The fix for the "infinite exploration" failure mode — directly prevents unscoped reads from filling context.

**Direct blast-radius / impact queries.**
Ask precise dependency questions instead of grepping by hand: "What would break if I change the signature of `authenticate` on `UserService`? List every caller, group by package, flag positional-argument callers." ([developertoolkit](https://developertoolkit.ai/en/claude-code/tips-tricks/large-codebase/), [agiinprogress](https://agiinprogress.substack.com/p/mastering-claude-code-plan-mode-the))
*When/why:* Quantify the impact of a specific change at the Research → Plan boundary.

### Plan

**Let Claude interview you, then write a self-contained `SPEC.md`.**
Start minimal and ask Claude to interview you with the AskUserQuestion tool about implementation, UI/UX, edge cases, and tradeoffs, then write a complete spec. The best specs "name the files and interfaces involved, state what is out of scope, and end with an end-to-end verification step." Then start a fresh session to execute it. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))
*When/why:* Turns a vague backlog idea into a precise, reviewable artifact — and surfaces decisions you hadn't considered.

**Edit the plan as a durable, version-controlled artifact.**
Press Ctrl+G to open the proposed plan in your editor and refine it before any code is written — the cheapest moment to catch missing requirements. Practitioners move plan/spec files out of `~/.claude/plans/` into the repo so they're reviewable across sessions and reusable to recover after errors. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [numustafa](https://numustafa.medium.com/claude-code-real-workflows-plan-mode-specs-f196fb0c3590), [alexop](https://alexop.dev/posts/spec-driven-development-claude-code-in-action/))

**Three-document chain with a review gate between each (spec → plan → code).**
Each gate catches a distinct failure: spec review catches scope creep, plan review catches half-finished stubs and conflicting patterns, code review catches plans that break on first contact with a failing test. GitHub's Spec Kit formalizes this as slash commands (`/speckit.specify` → `/speckit.clarify` → `/speckit.plan` → `/speckit.tasks` → `/speckit.implement`). ([DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/spec-driven-development-with-claude-code), [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit))
*When/why:* Pays off for large refactors, migrations, and unclear requirements; overkill for small fixes (see the skip rule).

**Classify the task: async-autonomous vs. synchronous-supervised.**
Anthropic's teams decide the run mode before starting: peripheral/prototyping work runs well asynchronously with auto-accept; core business logic and critical fixes need synchronous oversight. ([Anthropic teams](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/58284b19e702b49db9302d5b6f135ad8871e7658.pdf))

### Build

**Write a lean, pruned `CLAUDE.md` (and run `/init` to seed it).**
Loaded every session, so it must earn its tokens: bash commands Claude can't infer, non-default style rules, test runner, repo etiquette, gotchas. Litmus test per line: "Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes? If not, cut it." Target under ~200 lines; bloat causes Claude to *ignore* your actual instructions. Anthropic's teams refine it continuously (e.g. asking Claude at session end to suggest improvements). ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), [Anthropic teams](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/58284b19e702b49db9302d5b6f135ad8871e7658.pdf))
*Important nuance:* `CLAUDE.md` is delivered as a user message, not the system prompt — it shapes but does not *enforce* behavior. For must-happen-every-time rules, use a hook instead.

**Reference existing patterns and exact sources in prompts.**
"Look at how widgets are implemented; `HotDogWidget.php` is a good example; follow that pattern." For bugs: symptom + likely location + what "fixed" looks like. Feed context via `@`-files, pasted screenshots, allowlisted doc URLs, or piped data (`cat error.log | claude`). ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [common workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows))

**Clean-git + checkpoint-heavy autonomous prototyping ("try and rollback").**
Start from a clean git state, enable auto-accept, set up an autonomous loop, then review the ~80% solution. Anthropic's data-science team treats it "like a slot machine — let Claude work autonomously for 30 minutes, and either accept the solution or restart fresh." ([Anthropic teams](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/58284b19e702b49db9302d5b6f135ad8871e7658.pdf))

**The three-attempt framework.**
Sanity's staff engineer: attempt 1 is mostly wrong but reveals the real challenges, attempt 2 understands the nuances, attempt 3 is a workable starting point. Reframes early bad output as process, not failure. ([Sanity](https://www.sanity.io/blog/first-attempt-will-be-95-garbage))

**Course-correct early; `/clear` and checkpoint.**
Esc to interrupt (context preserved), Esc+Esc / `/rewind` to restore state. After two failed corrections on the same issue, `/clear` and rewrite a better prompt — a clean session almost always beats a long polluted one. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))

**Capture discoveries mid-task and fold them back.**
incident.io uses a `/note_this` slash command to append discoveries to feature notes, later promoted into `CLAUDE.md`. Combats Claude's lack of cross-session memory. ([incident.io](https://incident.io/blog/using-claude-to-power-up-your-onboarding))

**Hooks for deterministic guardrails.**
A `PostToolUse` hook auto-formats on every edit; a `PreToolUse` hook blocks edits to protected paths (`.env`, `.git/`) or destructive commands by exiting code 2 (stderr is fed back to Claude). Hooks are shell commands, not prompts, so the model can't forget. ([hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [hooks guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide), [pixelmojo](https://www.pixelmojo.io/blogs/claude-code-hooks-production-quality-ci-cd-patterns))

### Verify

**Give Claude a check it can run — the single highest-leverage practice.**
Provide a pass/fail signal Claude reads in-conversation: test suite, build exit code, linter, fixture diff, or screenshot diff. "Claude does the work, runs the check, reads the result, and iterates until the check passes." Escalation ladder: in-prompt → a `/goal` condition re-checked each turn → a Stop hook that blocks the turn until the check passes (overridden after 8 consecutive blocks). Demand evidence (test output, command results), not assertions of success. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [agent loop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop))

**Test-driven development as an external oracle.**
TDD is repeatedly called the strongest verification pattern because each red→green cycle gives unambiguous feedback that "stays accurate regardless of how long the session has been running." For bugs: "write a failing test that reproduces the issue, then fix it." Caveat: Claude defaults to writing implementation *before* tests, so test-first must be demanded explicitly. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [Anthropic teams blog](https://claude.com/blog/how-anthropic-teams-use-claude-code), [TDD guide](https://github.com/FlorianBruniaux/claude-code-ultimate-guide/blob/main/guide/workflows/tdd-with-claude.md))

**Adversarial review in a fresh context (Writer/Reviewer).**
Before counting work done, have a fresh-context subagent (or the bundled `/code-review` skill) review the diff against `PLAN.md`, seeing only the diff and criteria — "a fresh context improves code review since Claude won't be biased toward code it just wrote." Important caveat: a reviewer told to find gaps "will usually report some, even when the work is sound... Chasing every finding leads to over-engineering." Scope it to correctness/requirement gaps. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))

**Layered review: Claude self-review → human → team.**
Sanity runs Claude self-review (coverage/bugs), then human review (architecture, business logic, integration), then normal team review. AI handles the mechanical first pass (security, style/arch conformance, test adequacy); humans keep acceptance and strategy. Roll out in phases: shadow mode first, then block only critical findings. ([Sanity](https://www.sanity.io/blog/first-attempt-will-be-95-garbage), [alirezarezvani](https://alirezarezvani.medium.com/5-tipps-to-automate-your-code-reviews-with-claude-code-5becd60bce5c))

**Dedicated security review.**
Run `/security-review` before committing, or wire up the `claude-code-security-review` GitHub Action — diff-aware, posts inline PR comments, auto-filters low-impact false positives. Caveat: it "is not hardened against prompt injection attacks and should only be used to review trusted PRs." ([security review](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-security-review), [official action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/claude-code-action-official))

### Share

**Commit and open the PR via `gh`.**
Install the `gh` CLI so Claude can open PRs and read comments without hitting unauthenticated rate limits. Creating the PR with `gh` auto-links the session (resume with `claude --from-pr <number>`). Ask Claude to highlight risks before submitting. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [common workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows))

**Headless mode + a three-layer governance loop into CI.**
`claude -p "prompt"` runs non-interactively with `--output-format json` and `--allowedTools` for scoped, unattended runs. The recommended end-to-end pattern: `CLAUDE.md` defines standards, hooks enforce them locally, and the same gates (lint, type-check, security) re-run in CI so AI-generated code meets the same bar as human code. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [pixelmojo](https://www.pixelmojo.io/blogs/claude-code-hooks-production-quality-ci-cd-patterns))

**Write back to the tracker and persist learnings.**
Close the loop without leaving the terminal ("Add a comment to ENG-456 with implementation details, then transition to In Review"). Use auto memory / the `#` key for machine-local notes, and "add this to CLAUDE.md" for team-shared learnings, feeding the next Pick. ([builder.io](https://www.builder.io/blog/claude-code-with-jira), [memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory))

## The two techniques the speaker is considering

### (a) Prompt engineering / meta-prompting — **Supported, with first-party tooling**

The research strongly supports this, and Anthropic ships dedicated tooling for it. How practitioners actually do it:

- **Generate a prompt from scratch.** The [Metaprompt cookbook](https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/misc-metaprompt) and the Console [prompt generator](https://claude.com/blog/prompt-generator) feed Claude a long multishot prompt of exemplars and your task, returning a structured template (role, chain-of-thought scratchpad, XML structure, examples). Solves the "blank page problem"; explicitly a starting point to iterate on.
- **Improve an existing prompt.** The Console [prompt improver](https://claude.com/blog/prompt-improver) rewrites a draft by adding a reasoning section, standardizing examples into XML, and fixing structure — reporting a ~30% accuracy lift on a multilabel classification task.
- **Let Claude write its own scaffolding.** The interview-to-`SPEC.md` flow is meta-prompting in practice — Claude generates the instructions for its own build phase. So is `/init` generating a starter `CLAUDE.md`, and Claude authoring hooks, `SKILL.md` files, and subagent definitions. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))
- **Offload example curation.** Ask Claude to evaluate your few-shot examples for relevance/diversity or generate more (3–5, diverse, wrapped in `<example>` tags). ([prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices))

**Caveat to feature, not bury:** auto-generated prompts can carry *deprecated* patterns. The prompt improver historically suggested an assistant **prefill**, but prefilled responses on the last assistant turn are no longer supported on Claude 4.6+ (return a 400 error). And older "CRITICAL: You MUST" emphasis now causes **over-triggering** on newer models — dial it back to normal "Use this tool when..." phrasing. Review any Claude-generated prompt against current model guidance. ([prompt improver](https://claude.com/blog/prompt-improver), [Claude 4 best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices))

### (b) Data-mining Confluence / JIRA / source code / Slack (incl. architecture & ADR extraction) — **Supported, via MCP and parallel subagents**

The research supports this strongly. The dominant mechanic is **search-then-fetch over MCP**, plus parallel subagent enrichment, with a human review gate.

- **Connect via the Atlassian / Slack / GitHub MCP servers.** The official Atlassian Remote MCP server (OAuth, hosted) "respects all your existing permission controls" — Claude only sees what the authenticated user can. The payoff: Claude can "walk Jira, GitHub, and Confluence in one pass," pulling a ticket, its linked design docs, related issues, and code into one context window. ([Atlassian](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/announcements/remote-mcp-server), [MCP announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol), [jaydengames](https://www.jaydengames.com/posts/claude-code-mcp-ultimate-workflow/))
- **Search-then-fetch, not space-dumping.** Run a CQL/JQL search to find candidates, then fetch full content only for the relevant ones (`confluence_search` + `confluence_get_page`, `jira_search` + `jira_get_issue`). This is the just-in-time retrieval style Anthropic's context-engineering guidance favors. **Mine page comments and edit history** — that's where "we tried X and it broke" lives. ([sooperset/mcp-atlassian](https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian), [effective context engineering](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents))
- **Parallel multi-source enrichment (the CLUE pattern).** Anthropic's security team built CLUE: an orchestrator fans out subagents querying Slack, internal docs, code, and data warehouses in parallel, each returning a condensed summary — ~25 tool calls and ~11 queries per investigation, "beyond manual capacity." ([Anthropic cybersecurity](https://claude.com/blog/how-anthropic-uses-claude-cybersecurity))
- **Mining Slack recovers the "why."** Search by date/user/keyword, then synthesize scattered messages into a decision record — catching *implicit* decisions like "yeah we should add rate limiting before launch" that keyword search misses. Slack's own engineering bot (RAG over chat + docs + canvases) saved an estimated 3,000+ hours. ([Slack MCP](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/), [samuellawrentz](https://samuellawrentz.com/blog/claude-code-slack-linear-mcp/), [slack.engineering](https://slack.engineering/empowering-engineers-with-ai/))
- **Architecture & ADR extraction works — as a draft.** Two patterns: (1) scan the codebase against an ADR template to generate records, and capture decisions live with a `/record-adr` command; (2) derive C4 / dependency / mermaid diagrams from *structured* signals (AST graphs, repo maps) rather than raw code dumps, refined over a few correction passes. Keep a tiny `CLAUDE.md` index of numbered ADRs and load only the relevant ones before planning. ([adolfi.dev](https://adolfi.dev/blog/ai-generated-adr/), [7tonshark](https://7tonshark.com/posts/claude-adr-pattern/), [beyondautocomplete](https://www.beyondautocomplete.nl/how-i-use-claude-code-to-keep-my-architecture-decisions-on-track/), [dev.to](https://dev.to/anoop_kumar_paul/how-to-create-architecture-overviews-from-existing-code-3enm), [heuel.org](https://blog.heuel.org/2025/01/creating-architecture-diagrams-with-c4-and-ai/))

**Caveats to state plainly:**
- Read operations are reliable; **cross-tool write/automation workflows hit rate limits and auth friction** — practitioners note "native tool integrations often outperform MCP" for production, and realistic setup is "weeks to months." Keep the tool list short (~5–6 servers); the model weighs every tool on every turn. ([nimbalyst](https://nimbalyst.com/blog/claude-code-mcp-setup/), [jaydengames](https://www.jaydengames.com/posts/claude-code-mcp-ultimate-workflow/))
- **Context rot from internal wikis is real** — stale, duplicate, and contradictory pages cause poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash. Prefer recently-updated pages and ask Claude to flag conflicts. ([01.me](https://01.me/en/2025/12/context-engineering-from-claude/))
- **Always gate on human review, markdown-first.** Generate a local markdown draft, verify quotes/snippets against source pages, then publish. Extracted ADRs/diagrams are starting points: "Generated diagrams need human review. Always." ([ivandachev](https://ivandachev.com/blog/claude-code-mcp-atlassian-integration), [dev.to](https://dev.to/anoop_kumar_paul/how-to-create-architecture-overviews-from-existing-code-3enm))

## Pitfalls / what to watch

**The trust-then-verify gap (confident-but-wrong).** Claude produces plausible code and asserts "should work," "looks good," "probably fine." One practitioner shipped broken code three times in one week on the strength of "should work." Fix: always provide verification — "If you can't verify it, don't ship it." ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [chudi.dev](https://chudi.dev/blog/claude-code-complete-guide))

**Context pollution.** Named failure modes: the *kitchen-sink session* (unrelated tasks piled into one context), *correcting over and over* (context full of failed approaches), and *infinite exploration* (an unscoped "investigate X" reading hundreds of files). Fix: `/clear` between tasks; after two failed corrections, `/clear` and rewrite; scope investigations or push them to subagents. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))

**Bloated `CLAUDE.md` is self-defeating.** "Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions." If Claude keeps violating a rule, the file is too long. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))

**Scope creep and partial analysis.** Claude invents out-of-scope features (asked to streamline docs, it unprompted added a Discord group, support email, and "best practices") and refactors only *some* files while claiming a comprehensive review. Constrain scope with a spec and check that the *whole* change was actually made. ([kleiber.me](https://kleiber.me/blog/2025/10/12/claude-code-five-observations/))

**Reviewers over-report.** An adversarial reviewer asked to find gaps will find some even when work is sound — leading to over-engineering. Scope reviewers to correctness/requirements. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices))

**Tests verify only what you tested.** A green suite means the cases you wrote pass — not that the feature does what you asked. And the author of code shouldn't be the certifier of it (use a fresh context). ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [agent loop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop))

**Multi-agent is a poor fit for most coding.** Anthropic's orchestrator-subagent setup beat single-agent Opus by 90.2% on a *research* eval — but warns "most coding tasks involve fewer truly parallelizable tasks than research," and multi-agent burns ~15x the tokens of a single chat. A practitioner's 26-agent design "ran out of context in less than 15-20 minutes" with agents not referencing each other's work. For Build, prefer git-worktree isolation over true parallel coding. ([multi-agent research](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/built-multi-agent-research-system), [Ilyas Ibrahim](https://medium.com/@ilyas.ibrahim/how-i-made-claude-code-agents-coordinate-100-and-solved-context-amnesia-5938890ea825), [worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees))

**Team-scale anti-patterns.** Skill sprawl ("curation is the work; collection is the trap"), permission drift in `settings.json`, hook spam (floods get filtered, so important events get ignored), and "agent-blame postmortems" that fault the model instead of missing human controls. Treat skills/permissions as owned, quarterly-reviewed artifacts. (Figures are one blog's self-reported metrics.) ([digitalapplied](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/claude-code-anti-patterns-team-adoption-failure-modes-2026))

**Source staleness in setup guides.** The GitHub npm MCP server (`@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`) is deprecated as of April 2025 — use the remote HTTP server. Slack's MCP server is OAuth-remote-only despite guides showing local `npx`. Claude Code does **not** read `AGENTS.md` directly — import it with `@AGENTS.md` from `CLAUDE.md`. ([GitHub MCP install](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/installation-guides/install-claude.md), [Slack MCP](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/connect-to-claude/), [memory](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), [thepromptshelf](https://thepromptshelf.dev/blog/agents-md-vs-claude-md/))

### Conflicting advice — be honest about it

- **Emphasis: "IMPORTANT/YOU MUST" vs. dial it back.** Older best-practice advice recommends adding emphasis to improve adherence; the Claude 4 prompting doc says newer models *over-trigger* on aggressive language and you should soften it. Test against your actual model. ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices), [Claude 4 best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-4-best-practices))
- **Who owns the Plan phase.** Anthropic's internal data shows design/planning grew only 1%→9.9% — they *reserve* high-level design for humans. Sanity and incident.io actively push Claude into drafting specs and plans. ([Anthropic research](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-ai-is-transforming-work-at-anthropic), [Sanity](https://www.sanity.io/blog/first-attempt-will-be-95-garbage), [incident.io](https://incident.io/blog/using-claude-to-power-up-your-onboarding))
- **Does spec ceremony beat plain plan mode?** HN skeptics are unconvinced: "A detailed-enough spec is just code that you can't run," and demand measured evidence that spec-driven workflows beat plan mode without wasting tokens. A counter-view favors reusable, tested *skills* over agents that "improvise on every task." ([HN 48231575](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48231575), [HN 47467922](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47467922))
- **"Single-file changes only" is an outdated rule.** A `CLAUDE.md` rule forcing single-file refactors "may have helped an earlier model but would prevent a newer one from making coordinated cross-file edits." Keep changes scoped to one *intent*, and re-examine such configs every 3–6 months. ([large codebases](https://claude.com/blog/how-claude-code-works-in-large-codebases-best-practices-and-where-to-start))
- **Plan mode is soft-enforced.** A reverse-engineering analysis reports plan mode is implemented largely through prompt injection ("you MUST NOT make any edits"), not hard tool locks — treat it as workflow discipline, not a security boundary. ([Ronacher](https://lucumr.pocoo.org/2025/12/17/what-is-plan-mode/))
